subject: Tenant segmentation & SKU structure for Daylight Health private deployment
messages:
From: Megan Carter <megan.carter@daylighthealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwoodinc.com
Cc: Peter Lopez <peter.lopez@daylighthealth.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Clarify SKU vs tenant billing for our VPC deployment

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the platform looked promising. Before we move into a procurement review I need clarity on how Redwood expects us to model costs for our private VPC deployment. A couple of specific asks: 

- We plan to run three logical tenants in our VPC (prod, staging, analytics) sharing a dedicated cluster. Do you price per tenant or per node/slot?
- How is the platform fee applied for private deployments? Is it a flat annual fee per VPC, per customer, or per environment?
- Any precedent for a volume rebate if we commit to a 12‑18 month node reservation across clusters?

I've attached an expected usage spreadsheet with projected peak vGPU-hours. Can you share a sketch of SKU options and a sample term sheet so we can run this by procurement?

Thanks — cc'ing Peter (Eng) who will own sizing questions.

Attachment: daylight-expected-usage.xlsx

Best,
Megan Carter
Senior Infrastructure Program Manager
Daylight Health

From: marissa_cole@redwoodinc.com
To: Megan Carter <megan.carter@daylighthealth.com>
Cc: Peter Lopez <peter.lopez@daylighthealth.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify SKU vs tenant billing for our VPC deployment

Hi Megan — great questions. High-level answers first, then a suggested pricing sketch attached.

1) Pricing unit: for Private (VPC/on‑prem) we price at the infrastructure node level (reserved nodes / peak vGPU-hours) rather than per logical tenant. That avoids per-tenant metering complexity when customers run multiple namespaces on a shared cluster. You can treat your three logical tenants as namespaces; cost is determined by the capacity you reserve.

2) Platform fee: the platform fee is a single annual fee per VPC deployment (includes control plane, monitoring, and core feature entitlements). It is distinct from node licensing. Typical customers amortize it across environments; we can discuss staging exemptions.

3) Volume rebates: we do structured rebates for committed capacity. See attached sketch (marissa_daylight_term_sheet_v1.pdf) and a simple SKU matrix (sku_matrix.csv). Example banding: 0–2 reserved nodes = base price, 3–9 nodes = 7% rebate, 10+ nodes = 12% rebate. We also offer an early-adopter uplift rebate for first-year commitments (one-time 8% credit) for first deployments.

I've attached an annotated term sheet and a CSV that maps nodes -> supported qps and recommended support tiers. A few asks from our side to finalize numbers: 
- confirm which workloads must be isolated (prod vs analytics) — that changes whether we recommend separate clusters or tenancy within a single cluster
- confirm an initial committed node count and desired contract length (12 vs 18 vs 24 months)

If you want, we can do a 30-minute pricing working session later this week to walk through the spreadsheet.

Attachments: marissa_daylight_term_sheet_v1.pdf, sku_matrix.csv

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinc.com

From: marissa_cole@redwoodinc.com

Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 10:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Fwd: Clarify SKU vs tenant billing for our VPC deployment — pricing ask (Daylight Health)

Team — forwarding Daylight's usage and my initial sketch. Key negotiation points: 
- Customer expects to run prod + staging + analytics on same cluster if we can guarantee resource isolation. That pushes them to reserve higher peak capacity.
- They're asking for banded node rebates and potentially staging exemption from platform fee.
- Want final deliverable to include term sheet + redlined SOW for procurement.

Suggested approach: propose a tiered rebate (5/10/15) tied to committed vGPU-hours or reserved nodes, plus an early-adopter one-time credit for year 1. For platform fee, propose: full fee for prod VPC, 50% fee for staging if they insist on separate environment, or waive platform fee for staging if they agree to treat staging as a lower-priority namespace (no SLA).

Can you take a pass on numbers and an ops sentence that explains how we enforce tenant isolation on a shared cluster? I'll align on support tier options.

Forwarded message included below.

From: karthik_iyer@redwoodinc.com
To: marissa_cole@redwoodinc.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinc.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinc.com
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarify SKU vs tenant billing for our VPC deployment — pricing ask (Daylight Health)

Marissa — here's a concrete, defensible pricing counter we can use in the working session. Copying ops language you can reuse in the SOW.

Pricing proposal (example numbers for negotiation):
- Node licensing (per reserved node per month): $9,500 / node / month (12-mo commit).
- Volume rebates (applied to node licensing): 3–5 nodes = 5% rebate, 6–11 nodes = 10% rebate, 12+ nodes = 15% rebate.
- Early-adopter credit: one-time 8% credit applied to first 12 months if they sign within 30 days.
- Platform fee: $55,000 / year per VPC. Staging concession: waive platform fee for staging if they commit to >= 6 nodes total and accept lower SLA for non-prod namespaces.
- Support tiers: Tier 2 (business hours + 4hr P1 response + optional oncall): add $7,500 / month. Tier 3 (24/7 oncall, 1hr P1): add $18,000 / month. We recommend Tier 3 for production-critical workloads.

Operations note for SOW (tenant isolation):
"Redwood will enforce logical tenant isolation using namespace-level resource quotas, node taints/tolerations, and cgroup-based CPU/GPU allocation. For environments requiring strict hardware isolation (regulatory or compliance), separate node pools will be provisioned and billed as dedicated nodes in the SKU. Resource exhaustion protections include eviction policies and soft reservations per namespace."

Point to be mindful of: procurement may push for per-tenant pricing — we should stick to node-based to keep billing predictable and easier to audit. The staging waiver is a good tactical move if Daylight cares about initial cash flow.

Happy to drop these numbers into the term sheet and SOW.

karthik
